blocks.prompt: 6. Is 301 a term of the A.P. \(5, 11, 17, \ldots\)?
blocks.explanation:
Sawal yeh hai ke kya 301 is list mein kahin aata hai ya nahi.
Agar aata hai to us ki position \(n\) ek positive whole number (1, 2, 3, ...) hogi.
Plan: \(a_n = 301\) rakh kar \(n\) nikalna, phir dekhna ke \(n\) poora number hai ya fraction.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(5, 11, 17, \ldots\)
Humein find karna hai: kya 301 is A.P. ki term hai?
Tareeqa: General term \(a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d\). Koi number tabhi term hai jab \(a_n = 301\) se \(n\) natural number aaye. Yeh test is liye theek hai ke \(n\) term ka number (position) hai, aur positions sirf 1, 2, 3, ... hoti hain.

General term nikalein
\[a_1 = 5,\quad d = 11 - 5 = 6\]
\[a_n = 5 + (n - 1)6 = 6n - 1\]
Kyun: Bracket khola to \(5 + 6n - 6 = 6n - 1\). Choti si check: \(n = 1\) par \(6 - 1 = 5\), jo pehli term hai.

\(a_n = 301\) rakhein
\[6n - 1 = 301\]
\[6n = 302\]
\[n = \dfrac{302}{6} = \dfrac{151}{3} = 50\tfrac{1}{3}\]
Kyun: \(n\) aadha ya teesra hissa nahi ho sakta; \(50\tfrac{1}{3}\)th term ka koi matlab nahi. Is liye 301 list mein nahi hai.
Dhyan dein: Kuch students \(n\) ko round kar ke 50 likh dete hain aur kehte hain 'haan, 50th term'. Yeh ghalat hai; round karna mana hai.

Tasdeeq: padosi terms dekhein
\[a_{50} = 6(50) - 1 = 299\]
\[a_{51} = 6(51) - 1 = 305\]
Kyun: List 299 se seedha 305 par chhalang lagati hai; 301 beech mein reh jata hai. Is se humara 'nahi' wala jawab pakka ho gaya.
